geo.label: growth scare, cuts still priced
parts: Macro Stance

Bearish. The tape is pricing a growth problem, not an overheated economy. The Nasdaq 100 closed at 19,430.95 on March 10, down 3.81% in the prior session and 9.59% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Axios called it the worst day of 2025 for stocks as recession fears rose [[n11343]]. Goldman Sachs cut its US forecasts because tariff impacts are growing 'considerably more adverse' [[n10896]], and Morgan Stanley's Wilson warns the S&P 500 could sink 5% on growth risks [[n4060]]. The labour data gave the bears their evidence: February payrolls rose 151,000, less than expected [[n10827]]. Powell says the Fed is in no hurry to adjust rates while policy uncertainty runs this high [[n11257]], so the market is doing the easing itself.
Rates & Curve

The two-year Treasury yield closed the prior session at 3.89% and the ten-year at 4.22%, leaving the 10Y-2Y spread at +33 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-10). Over 20 observations the 2Y fell 40 bps and the 10Y fell 27 bps, so the spread widened 13 bps. The curve is positively sloped and the move is bull steepening (both down, 2Y down more) (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-10). That is the market buying rate cuts, not a bond rout. Equity fear shows in the VIX at 27.86, up 19.21% in the prior session and 68.44% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The S&P 500 closed at 5,614.56, down 6.83% over 20 sessions, and the dollar index sits at 103.91 index points after a 3.82% fall over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).
New / Most Important

The important shift is that the sell-off has moved from valuation to growth. Reuters reported US stocks losing $4 trillion in value as Trump plowed ahead on tariffs [[n0508]], and the White House pushed back on recession talk as household worries grew and stocks tanked [[n10944]]. Bloomberg counted $1.1 trillion wiped from the Nasdaq 100 as the tech meltdown spread [[n11328]]. Two tests come next. Yahoo Finance put the odds of a government shutdown this weekend at about 1 in 3 [[n11352]], and Trump said a shutdown is possible but expected to be averted [[n11287]]. Reuters framed the week ahead as a test of the stock market on inflation data [[n0499]]. Powell has signalled possible tweaks to the dot plot [[n11235]], while Waller still sees room for two to three cuts in 2025 [[n11158]].
Playbook ✓

Stay defensive on US beta into the shutdown and inflation tests. Keep index hedges in place rather than selling into weakness, favour cash-generative names with limited tariff exposure, and own duration while the curve bull-steepens, since TLT and IEF both rose over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The call changes if the Nasdaq 100 reclaims its 21,491.31 reference close from 2025-02-07 and the VIX falls back toward its 16.54 level from early February. That would mean the recession trade is unwinding rather than building (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).

geo.label: fiscal pivot, easing bias
parts: Macro Stance

Bullish, on the fiscal pivot more than on the growth data. The ECB cut its key rate to 2.5% and said policy is becoming 'meaningfully less restrictive' [[n3463]][[n3468]]. Germany is the bigger story. Euronews framed its fiscal boost as a 'whatever it takes' moment that sparked a market rally [[n3537]], and Merz has 2 weeks to deliver the spending revolution [[n3536]]. JPMorgan has joined Goldman in raising its euro-area growth forecast for 2025 [[n3616]], in the same week Goldman cut its US forecasts [[n10896]]. The Bundesbank's caveat, that more German spending is justified but 'not a cure-all', is the one to respect [[n3624]].
Credit & Inflation

The rate story here is a bond story. A German bond selloff spread through global markets [[n3474]][[n3451]], and fund managers are calling it a once-in-a-generation move [[n3540]]. The euro has done the heavy lifting: EUR/USD closed at 1.0861, up 4.29% over five sessions and 5.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Equities show a German-led rotation rather than a broad rally. The DAX closed at 22,620.95, up 3.24% over 20 sessions. The STOXX Europe 600 closed at 546.20, down 3.01% over five sessions and only 0.05% higher over 20 sessions, while the Euro Stoxx 50 rose 0.54% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The narrow gain is the point: the rally is in Germany and in defence.
New / Most Important

Berlin said no to joint defence Eurobonds and proposed funding joint projects through the EU budget instead [[n3609]]. That keeps the defence build-out national, which suits German primes and the hedge funds already holding them [[n3613]]. The Europe CEOs who will rethink their US pivot after the spending plan are the ones to watch [[n3556]]. The tariff overhang sits on the car makers. Volkswagen and Stellantis evaded Trump's 25% tariffs while BMW braces for impact [[n5006]], and Germany's car industry is bracing for the same tariffs [[n3542]].
Playbook ✓

Bullish on European cyclicals with German fiscal exposure, bought on pullbacks rather than chased. Prefer the DAX to the broader STOXX 600 while the rotation stays German-led. Keep auto exposure tactical until the tariff picture clears, and avoid adding to defence after Rheinmetall's 53.08% gain over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The stance changes if the German bond selloff pushes global long yields higher while the DAX gives back its 20-session gain, because that would turn the fiscal story into a funding problem.

geo.label: deflation persists, stimulus lags
parts: Macro Stance

Mixed. Deflation is the story the official numbers keep telling. Inflation fell below zero for the first time in a year [[n1505]], and CNN says China's deflation problems are getting worse [[n1547]]. Beijing's answer is a $41 billion consumption plan that CNBC calls 'just a start' [[n1539]]. The listed market is leaning the other way. The Hang Seng closed at 23,783.49, up 10.51% over 20 sessions, and the Shanghai Composite closed at 3,366.16 index points, up 1.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Growth is weak but the policy floor is visible, which is why the view is Mixed rather than Bearish.
PMIs & Activity

The most recent trade print shows the external engine stalling. Exports missed forecasts as US tariffs hit, and imports posted their sharpest decline since July 2023 [[n1325]]. JD.com topped revenue estimates on robust demand and government stimulus [[n1324]], which shows the stimulus reaching consumers in pockets. Until the next factory survey lands, the honest read is that activity is stabilising at a low level rather than accelerating. The trade figures are the test of whether tariffs or domestic demand dominate.
Credit Impulse

Credit is not accelerating yet. Bond yields jumped to three-month highs as investors pared rate-cut bets [[n1533]], and a strategist warns that more Chinese bond issuance to keep yields up will 'drain liquidity' from markets [[n4075]]. The state is funding growth in other ways, with a national venture capital guidance fund being set up [[n1322]]. Higher yields are the wrong direction for a deflation-hit economy, so the credit read stays negative until rate-cut expectations come back.
Property

Officials are talking property up. A minister says the sector shows positive changes [[n1504]], and another says the real estate market keeps stabilising as policy support boosts confidence [[n1507]]. The policy lever under discussion is the price cap on local governments buying apartments, which China mulls ending, Bloomberg News reports [[n1320]]. The rental market is still struggling with dwindling expatriate and corporate demand [[n1548]], and luxury brands keep closing outlets as spending shrinks [[n1514]]. Stabilisation is a claim until sales confirm it.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

The fiscal number that matters is the $41 billion consumption plan [[n1539]], which CNBC frames as a start against deflationary pressure. Protectionism is on the official agenda, with 2025 economic priorities set out while protectionism is 'on the rise' [[n1169]]. The trade fight is spreading to third countries. China hit back at Canada with fresh agriculture tariffs [[n1479]], and Chinese rapeseed meal and oil contracts surged after 100% tariffs on Canadian imports [[n1550]]. Washington is pushing back with a port fee on China's maritime trade [[n1623]]. The diplomacy channel is still open: Trump may meet Xi in China as soon as April, SCMP's insiders say [[n1556]], and Reuters reports the two sides discussing a Trump-Xi summit for June [[n1625]].
Markets & Flows

Mainland money is buying what foreigners are selling. Hedge funds cut China stocks for a fourth week as DeepSeek optimism faded [[n1564]], while mainland investors snapped up a record amount of Hong Kong stocks to play AI [[n1575]]. Prices confirm the split. KWEB closed at 35.41 USD, up 9.29% over 20 sessions, FXI at 35.97 USD, up 9.90%, and the Hang Seng rose 10.51% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Onshore, the Shanghai Composite rose 1.32% over 20 sessions and the CSI 300 ETF ASHR gained 0.98%. The yuan is steady, with USD/CNY at 7.2340, down 0.72% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).
New / Most Important

The signal that matters is the gap between a deflating economy and a rallying listed market. Deflation is still deepening [[n1547]], while a portfolio manager argues China is only now starting to have the AI-driven rally the US enjoyed for the last two years [[n1605]]. Alibaba is the bellwether, up 28.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), and Alibaba's new RISC-V chip is reported to hit the mark for China's tech ambitions [[n1568]]. Equity strength is coming from tech, not from the consumer or property sectors that the deflation data describe. That split matters for positioning because mainland money is the marginal buyer while foreign funds are the sellers, and a reversal in that flow would tell you more about China's direction than any single print.
Playbook ✓

Own Hong Kong AI and internet exposure through KWEB or FXI on pullbacks, not onshore, where the 20-session gain is smaller. Keep the yuan as a stability asset: USD/CNY at 7.2340, down 0.72% over 20 sessions, argues against paying for dollar protection. The call turns defensive if the Hang Seng gives back its 20-session gain while the deflation prints deepen. ⚠ Divergence: the Hang Seng's 10.51% gain over 20 sessions sits against deflation that is still deepening and a fourth week of hedge-fund selling in China stocks.

geo.label: hike bets, soft growth
parts: Macro Stance

Mixed. The Bank of Japan is being pushed toward a hike, and the bond market has taken the bets at face value. The 10-year yield hit its highest since 2008 on bets for BOJ hikes [[n5384]]. The economy is softer than that implies. Japan revised fourth-quarter GDP lower, complicating the BOJ's rate outlook [[n3112]], with US tariffs clouding the outlook [[n5387]]. The service-sector mood has soured on rising living costs [[n5389]], and officials urge vigilance on inflation and the rate impact [[n5388]]. Sources say the BOJ could discuss a hike in May [[n5310]]. Wages are the inflation risk, with the largest union group seeking its biggest wage-hike demand in over 30 years [[n5313]]. The yen is also bought as a haven, and one strategist calls it the new safe-haven currency [[n5355]].
Activity & Currency

USD/JPY closed at 147.6080, down 2.79% over 20 sessions and 2.10% over five sessions, as the yen firmed (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The Nikkei 225 closed at 37,028.27, down 5.22% over 20 sessions, while the Japan ETF EWJ at 68.68 USD gained 0.29% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The divergence is inside the index. SoftBank closed at 8,067.00 JPY, down 17.40% over 20 sessions, and Tokyo Electron at 21,475.00 JPY, down 19.21% over the same period, while Advantest rose 3.74% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Yen strength hurts exporters, and the chip and AI names carry most of the drawdown.
Playbook ✓

Mixed. Keep Japanese equity exposure near benchmark, favour domestic-demand names over exporters while the yen is firm, and wait for the May discussion before adding. The view turns bullish on exporters if USD/JPY climbs back above its 151.8460 reference from 2025-02-10, which would show the haven bid fading. It turns bearish if the Nikkei stays below its 39,066.53 reference close from 2025-02-06, because that would mean the market is pricing the hike and the slowdown together (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).

geo.label: rate cuts, fragile demand
parts: Macro Stance

Bearish. Australia is being squeezed from outside and inside. The RBA is weighing a series of global storms [[n0373]], and it used a 'secret chart' to justify its latest rate cut [[n0278]]. The owner of Country Road says Australia is stuck in a retail recession [[n0297]]. The tariff overhang is closing in: Trump vowed to take 'hundreds of billions' in tariffs as Australia's hopes of an exemption faded [[n1612]]. Chinese demand is cracking at the margin, with China's steel output cuts piling pressure on iron ore [[n0395]]. Savers are asking what happened to their rates after the cut [[n0346]].
Demand & Financing

AUD/USD closed at 0.6304, up 1.34% over five sessions but only 0.72% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 7,962.30, down 3.44% over five sessions and 6.14% over 20 sessions. The AFR says the ASX sell-off is getting serious and blames banks and passive investing [[n0376]], while BlackRock has cut its exposure to Australian shares, citing their poor value [[n0404]]. CBA closed at 148.14 AUD, down 9.02% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), so the bank has fallen further than the index. A feud over Australian banks was also a factor in the RBNZ governor's abrupt exit [[n0315]], which keeps the sector trading on sentiment.
Playbook ✓

Bearish. Underweight the banks and keep ASX exposure below benchmark until the S&P/ASX 200 reclaims its 8,482.80 reference close from 2025-02-10. That reclaim would show the sell-off was positioning rather than repricing, and it would justify moving back to neutral. Watch iron ore as the second trigger. Further Chinese steel cuts hit miners' earnings harder than the index, so the Australian dollar's 1.34% gain over five sessions should not be read as a demand signal (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).

geo.label: strong zloty, defence build-out
parts: Macro Stance

Mixed. Labour is the strength and the zloty is the question. Eurostat says Poland hit its lowest unemployment rate on record and is joint-lowest in the EU [[n5482]], and manufacturing shows signs of recovery for the first time in almost three years [[n5472]]. The currency has been fed by the central bank: the zloty surged to a 10-year high in late February, fanned by a hawkish central bank [[n5446]]. Money.pl asks what the limits for the zloty are and gathers three experts' forecasts [[n6043]]. Mortgage costs are easing, and Business Insider Polska says a confluence of favourable circumstances is bringing down the instalments Poles pay on housing loans [[n6047]]. GUS data reported on March 10 show that wages peak for the 35 to 44 age group [[n6118]].
Markets

USD/PLN closed at 3.8297, down 4.37% over five sessions and 5.70% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN closed at 4.1592, down 0.70% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Polish equities have outperformed the currency over 20 sessions. The iShares MSCI Poland ETF EPOL closed at 26.44 USD, up 8.81%, and the WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 49.19 PLN, up 3.23% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Leadership is rotating. Orlen gained 14.37% over 20 sessions to 64.80 PLN, Asseco Poland rose 15.79% to 142.30 PLN and mBank 10.04% to 741.20 PLN, while KGHM fell 8.57% to 128.00 PLN and JSW 5.27% to 23.38 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Dino Polska's shares have hit a record high [[n5979]]. Bankier asks who is bothered by a strong zloty, a currency that has been this strong only once in history [[n5992]].
Fiscal & Politics

Brussels is easing the excessive-deficit rules, and the question for Warsaw is whether Poland gains or loses [[n5913]]. Politics is less comfortable. A far-right candidate has jumped to second in the presidential race, Bloomberg reports [[n5535]], and an opposition MP was detained over alleged financial crimes [[n5510]]. Biejat says that, as president, she would tidy up the mortgage market [[n6057]], which makes housing finance an election issue. Washington says it will retaliate if Poland introduces a tax on big tech [[n5546]], and the Rubio exchange over the Ukraine Starlink spat adds friction [[n5525]].
Corporate & Sectors

Banks are the sector under the spotlight. Bankier reports that BIK scoring may limit competition in banking, and UOKiK is investigating [[n6091]]. Deposit rates are falling while banks earn billions [[n6078]], and Business Insider Polska says banks are again becoming punchbags as big profits become inconvenient [[n5917]]. PKO closed at 70.80 PLN, up 5.08% over 20 sessions, while Pekao fell 3.68% in the prior session to 169.00 PLN (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), so the sector is split. Energy is the policy-driven leg. Naftogaz and Orlen are to cooperate in LNG [[n5519]], and power is dear because CO2 costs are pushing prices up [[n5916]]. Mining is the stress point. KGHM's chief executive describes years of neglect and no investment [[n6024]]. Defence names are the speculative leg, with money moving from Ukrainian stocks into steel and armaments makers [[n6109]], and a military boom is earning for some listed companies [[n5996]]. Comarch will leave the WSE after more than 25 years with KNF's consent [[n5981]], and Cyfrowy Polsat is dropping out of the largest-company list [[n5983]].
Geopolitics & Security

Poland is building an army and talking nuclear options. Tusk announced military training for every adult man [[n5495]], and Poland asked NATO to raise its defence-spending minimum to 3% of GDP [[n5506]]. Politico reports Poland seeks access to nuclear arms and wants a half-million-man army [[n5507]], after the premier said Poland must look at nuclear options, alarmed by Trump [[n5493]]. Macron's nuclear-deterrent proposal was welcomed in Poland and the Baltics [[n5487]], and Russia is gearing up to build 100,000 drones a year on NATO's doorstep [[n5490]]. The defence money is real, but the export case is weaker. Money.pl argues Poland arms itself massively but does not earn on weapons [[n6112]].
New / Most Important

The signal that matters is a strong zloty meeting a defence build-out. Bankier's question about who is bothered by a strong currency [[n5992]] matters because the state is spending at the same moment. The Armament Agency has presented its plan for drones and air defence [[n5536]], which is where the money is heading. What it means: the spending is real and the currency is strong, but the industrial return is not yet proven, so the export question is the one to watch.
Playbook ✓

Mixed. Own Orlen for the energy and gas story, up 14.37% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), and stay light on the banks until the BIK competition probe clears. Trim defence speculation in the names that ran on the rotation out of Ukrainian stocks, and keep USD/PLN exposure small: the 5.70% fall over 20 sessions has already been the trade, and the forecasters disagree on the limits. The banks turn bullish if deposit rates keep falling while loan pricing holds. ⚠ Divergence: EPOL is up 8.81% over 20 sessions and the zloty is firmer, while the banks and KGHM are under pressure, so the market is paying for Poland's external story rather than its domestic earnings.
Narrative

Technology is where the sell-off hits the big growth funds hardest. XLK closed at 209.25 USD, down 4.25% in the prior session, 4.31% over five sessions and 10.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). NVIDIA has lost $1 trillion of market value and is down 20% this year [[n9318]], and one measure makes Nvidia cheaper than when ChatGPT launched after its 30% sell-off [[n6565]]. Apple is preparing a major software overhaul for iPhone, iPad and Mac [[n9123]]. The sector's drawdown is an AI-valuation story and a rates-and-tariffs story at the same time, and the second is harder to hedge.
Reported

Oracle closed at 148.79 USD, down 14.71% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Broadcom's rolling job cuts have roughly halved VMware's workforce [[n3130]], which is a cost story rather than a growth one.

Apple's software overhaul is the upside option [[n9123]]. The AI demand backdrop has a visible customer in OpenAI, which is paying CoreWeave $11.9 billion over five years for AI data-centre services [[n3125]]. Those are demand signals for the infrastructure layer rather than support for software multiples.

The consensus says AI capex keeps rising. Dan Niles says Oracle's AI capex will decline [[n9179]], which cuts against the cloud-infrastructure story that justified the group's multiples. Oracle is already down 14.71% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), so part of that call is already in the price.

The convention is that Costco's miss is the staples bear case [[n2995]]. Yet the sector is up over 20 sessions while Costco is down 10.48% over the same span at 934.41 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The defensive bid is rotating within staples, not into them.
Narrative

Health care is flat over 20 sessions, but the drug names are diverging. XLV closed at 147.67 USD, down 1.08% in the prior session and up 0.85% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Novo Nordisk shares fell 6.3% after the latest trial results for its next-generation weight-loss drug [[n9327]]. Eli Lilly closed at 829.76 USD, down 5.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), and Lilly plans to launch its weight-loss drug in emerging markets this year [[n4049]].
Reported

Xeris Biopharma rose to a nearly four-year high on a strong 2025 outlook [[n6426]], and Ocugen's Q4 revenue crushed estimates [[n6308]]. Illumina is cutting $100 million in costs and lowering guidance because of a China sales ban [[n3103]].
EPS Upside Watch
Lilly's emerging-market launch is the growth lever [[n4049]], and Roche is hiring a Novo executive to push into obesity drugs [[n9355]], which widens the field the set-up depends on.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that obesity demand is unstoppable. Barron's says the weight-loss drug surge is fading fast in the Hims & Hers case [[n6408]], and Hims & Hers is abandoning the Apostrophe dermatology business it paid $190 million for [[n6446]]. Novo is down 8.64% over 20 sessions at 78.95 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).
Narrative

Materials is where copper is treated as an asset and the miners are not. XLB closed at 85.99 USD, down 2.08% in the prior session and 2.61% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Copper closed at 4.64 USD per pound, up 1.27% over 20 sessions, while the copper-miners ETF COPX is down 6.22% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Copper here is an AI and grid asset, not a gauge of China's growth, and the miners are not yet getting the bid.
Reported
Meridian raised the value of its Cabaçal gold-copper project by 71% after a new study [[n9287]], and BHP is investing $25 million in copper explorer Cobre [[n0456]].
EPS Upside Watch

Iron ore is the squeeze. China's cuts to steel production are piling pressure on Australian iron ore [[n0395]], and Freeport closed at 34.50 USD, down 9.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Miners with iron-ore exposure carry that risk.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that copper strength lifts every miner. Fortescue is down 18.33% over 20 sessions at 15.86 AUD while copper rises (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), and US steel and aluminium tariffs are reshaping trade flows [[n1597]]. The miners are trading the tariff map, not the metal.
Narrative

Real estate is flat over 20 sessions and rate-sensitive in the prior session. XLRE closed at 42.06 USD, down 0.97% in the prior session and up 0.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Mortgage rates are falling: they reached their lowest point this year in early March [[n10666]], and rates are down 37 basis points this year [[n10863]]. The bond rally is doing the work that the equity sector cannot yet show.
Reported

Redfin's stock spiked after mortgage giant Rocket announced a $1.75 billion deal to buy the company [[n10923]], and the deal would consolidate home listings and mortgage lending in one place [[n10925]].
EPS Upside Watch

Mortgage originators with scale are the upside. Consolidating listings and lending [[n10925]] favours firms that can own the whole funnel, and falling rates [[n10863]] lift origination volumes without needing a sector rerating.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that falling mortgage rates help real estate. The sector is down 3.35% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), and the rate fall is arriving alongside a recession scare that the White House is pushing back on [[n10944]]. The rate relief is not yet a sector tailwind.
Narrative

Utilities are the defensive being bought for power demand, but the names are split. XLU closed at 78.14 USD, up 1.10% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). NextEra closed at 76.16 USD, up 11.56% over 20 sessions, while Constellation Energy fell 34.73% and Vistra fell 35.00% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The data-centre load story is real: PJM transmission growth has rebounded, and data centres boost the outlook for future expansion [[n10921]].
Reported
Hitachi Energy committed $250 million to address the transformer shortage [[n9243]], and Ontario raised US power prices by 25% for three states [[n9334]].
EPS Upside Watch
Grid capex is the upside. The transformer shortage [[n9243]] keeps regulated spending needs high, and the transmission rebound [[n10921]] says the build-out is not waiting for generators to arrive.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that data-centre demand is a pure windfall for power sellers. A Harvard Law paper argues utilities may subsidize data-center growth by shifting costs to other ratepayers [[n9409]], and the split in the names, with NextEra up and Constellation and Vistra down over 20 sessions, is consistent with that argument (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).
Narrative

European autos are a tariff trade. The sector ETF EXV5.DE closed at 53.14 EUR, up 1.33% in the prior session and 2.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Volkswagen's US listing is up 20.66% over 20 sessions to 12.03 USD, and BMW is up 11.19% to 85.66 EUR (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Volkswagen and Stellantis evaded Trump's 25% tariffs while BMW braces for impact [[n5006]], so the sector splits by exposure to the US rather than by country.
Reported

Porsche and Volkswagen will keep the dual CEO role until the restructuring is complete, WirtschaftsWoche reports [[n8743]]. Tesla's sales plummeted 45% in Europe [[n3032]], which is a share question for the European makers as much as a Tesla problem.
EPS Upside Watch

Domestic demand and fiscal spending are the upside. Merz's spending plan [[n3536]] is a domestic-demand option rather than an export one, and the car industry's own tariff bracing [[n3542]] caps the export upside.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that Trump's tariffs hurt every rival of Tesla equally. The New York Times argues the tariffs could help Tesla by hurting its rivals more [[n1613]], which cuts against the European makers' tariff-relief story.
Narrative

Semiconductors are the AI trade's barometer, and it is in drawdown. SOXX closed at 194.42 USD, down 4.63% in the prior session and 10.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). NVIDIA is down 17.61% over 20 sessions and Broadcom 17.97% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The demand story is intact: OpenAI is paying CoreWeave $11.9 billion over five years for AI data-centre services [[n3125]], and Broadcom's AI revenue jumped 77% [[n2988]].
Reported

Broadcom shares rose as strong guidance on AI growth powered the stock [[n2990]], and Barron's says the stock soared after the chip maker beat, with the AI trade not dead [[n2989]]. Marvell's shares tumbled despite an earnings beat [[n3008]].
EPS Upside Watch

Broadcom's guidance is the template for the group: an AI revenue print with strong guidance [[n2990]] that has not stopped the stock falling, down 17.97% over 20 sessions to 184.45 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The next beat that lifts guidance is the upside watch. A beat alone is not enough, as Marvell showed [[n3008]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that Nvidia owns AI silicon. The Financial Times reports inference is driving competition to Nvidia's dominance [[n9251]], and Huawei is reported to have acquired two million Ascend 910 AI chips from TSMC through shell companies [[n1570]]. The competition is in the chips and in the supply chain, and that is the breaker.

earnings_pattern.title: What the Market Pays For: forward numbers over the quarter
parts: Rewarded

Guidance that lifts the story gets paid. Broadcom's AI revenue jumped 77% and the stock jumped with it [[n2988]], and CNBC reports shares rose as strong guidance powered by AI growth [[n2990]]. Barron's says the stock soared after the chip maker beat, and that the AI trade is not dead [[n2989]]. Air France-KLM shares jumped on an earnings beat and growth expectations [[n2849]], and Rolls-Royce's full-year results beat expectations [[n3019]]. Among smaller names, Adma Biologics' retail holders eyed a higher open after a blowout Q4 [[n6122]], Ocugen's Q4 revenue crushed estimates [[n6308]], and Xeris rose to a nearly four-year high on a strong 2025 outlook [[n6426]]. Coforge shares jumped 10% after a large deal win [[n6259]]. Reddit's ad revenue is growing faster than other social platforms [[n3018]].
Punished

Misses and cut guidance get punished, especially in consumer names. Costco missed quarterly profit estimates on rising merchandise costs [[n2874]], and its stock fell as the retailer faced cautious consumers and tariff threats [[n2996]]. Marvell's shares tumbled despite an earnings beat [[n3008]], and HPE's stock crashed on job cuts, an earnings miss and DOGE [[n3004]]. AeroVironment tumbled after hours on a Q3 profit miss and a cut to its 2025 forecast [[n6126]]. Delta slashed its earnings outlook on weaker US demand, and its shares fell [[n3098]]. Illumina is lowering guidance because of a China sales ban [[n3103]], Novo Nordisk fell 6.3% on trial results [[n9327]], and Abercrombie was pummelled by a predicted tariff hit [[n6244]].
Pattern

Two things get paid: AI-linked revenue and guidance that holds. In the same stretch Broadcom's outlook lifted the group, while Delta, Illumina and Costco cut or missed, and the market read the cuts as a verdict on the consumer and on trade policy rather than on the individual companies. A beat without a higher outlook is not enough, as Marvell showed. The pattern punishes forward numbers that tariffs can reach.
Attention into EPS

The next prints carry the most risk where the outlook depends on tariffs. Abercrombie has already said a tariff hit is coming [[n6244]], and Foot Locker says the sneaker industry and Nike still have more pain ahead [[n0469]]. Enphase fell 7% after a sales and income drop [[n0468]]. Oracle's sales missed estimates while its chief executive expects AI-driven growth [[n0504]], and Dan Niles says Oracle's AI capex will decline [[n9179]]. Attention into the next prints is on whether AI capex guidance holds.
Playbook

Own the guidance raisers and avoid the cutters into the next prints. Broadcom is the template, Costco and Oracle are the cautions, and tariff-exposed retailers need a visible guidance cut to be priced. A flat outlook will be punished the way Marvell was. Positioning follows the outlook rather than the beat, so size earnings trades on the forward number.

underowned.title: Hong Kong AI and internet: global funds leave, mainland money arrives
parts: Attention Gap

Global funds have been selling China stocks for a fourth week [[n1564]], while mainland investors snapped up a record amount of Hong Kong stocks to play AI [[n1575]]. The buyers are mainland savers rather than the global funds that set the tone, so the theme is under-owned in the places that matter to Western benchmarks. Alibaba is up 28.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), so the move has been fast relative to the flows that funded it.
Exposure & Risk

KWEB at 35.41 USD, FXI at 35.97 USD and Alibaba at 132.54 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The risk is a deflation print that does not turn [[n1547]], and US port fees on Chinese shipping that escalate the trade fight [[n1623]].
Trigger to Watch
A Trump-Xi summit date would move the theme from under-owned to consensus. Reuters reports talk of a June summit [[n1625]], and SCMP's insiders say Trump may meet Xi as soon as April [[n1556]].

underowned.title: The yen as a haven: firm in the currency, bid in bonds
parts: Attention Gap

A strategist calls the yen the new safe-haven currency [[n5355]], and USD/JPY closed at 147.6080, down 2.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Japanese investors boosted bond holdings and sold foreign stocks in February [[n5390]]. The haven bid is showing up in both the currency and domestic bonds.
Exposure & Risk

USD/JPY and the Nikkei 225, which closed at 37,028.27, down 5.22% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). A firm yen squeezes exporters, and the chip names with the biggest yen exposure carry the most risk.
Trigger to Watch
BOJ sources point to a possible discussion of a hike in May [[n5310]]. A hawkish signal from that discussion would test whether the haven bid survives higher rates.

underowned.title: Copper miners: the grid metal nobody owns
parts: Attention Gap

Copper is an AI and grid asset, and the explorers get little attention. BHP is investing $25 million in copper explorer Cobre [[n0456]], Meridian raised the value of its gold-copper project by 71% [[n9287]], and IPT is hunting copper in Broken Hill [[n0429]]. Copper closed at 4.64 USD, up 1.27% over 20 sessions, while the miners' ETF COPX is down 6.22% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).
Exposure & Risk

COPX at 38.61 USD and Freeport at 34.50 USD, which is down 9.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Steel output cuts in China [[n0395]] and US steel and aluminium tariffs [[n1597]] are the risks.
Trigger to Watch
COPX reclaiming its 41.17 USD reference close from 2025-02-07 would show the miners moving with the metal again (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).

underowned.title: Data-centre power: utilities split by who pays
parts: Attention Gap

The market is pricing winners and losers within one data-centre story. NextEra is up 11.56% over 20 sessions, while Constellation Energy is down 34.73% and Vistra down 35.00% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The cost-shifting argument is now in print, in a Harvard Law paper on utilities subsidizing data-center growth [[n9409]].
Exposure & Risk

NextEra closed at 76.16 USD, Constellation Energy at 202.21 USD and Vistra at 108.49 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The risk is a ratepayer backlash that turns the cost argument into rate cases.
Trigger to Watch
PJM transmission growth and the data-centre outlook [[n10921]] keep the demand story alive. The trigger is a cost-allocation fight that moves from papers into regulatory filings.

crypto.title: Crypto & Digital Assets: the reserve bid meets a 20-session drawdown
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 78,532.00 USD, down 2.57% in the prior session and 17.80% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-10). Ether fell 30.28% over 20 sessions to 1,861.15 USD, Solana fell 30.04% to 118.29 USD and XRP fell 21.13% to 2.02 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-10). The equity proxies fell further. Coinbase closed at 179.23 USD, down 34.70% over 20 sessions, Strategy at 239.27 USD, down 26.95%, and the iShares bitcoin trust IBIT at 44.91 USD, down 17.55% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The brokerage Robinhood is down 36.22% at 35.63 USD over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).
New / Most Important

Bitcoin fell to a November low under $80,000 on heightened recession fears [[n2023]]. Trump signed an order establishing a strategic bitcoin reserve [[n1971]], yet Bitcoin fell as much as 6.5% as volatility continued after the reserve plan [[n2004]]. The reserve is the bull case retail is repeating: Trump pledged a 'digital Fort Knox' [[n1969]], and Stocktwits says retail remains bullish even as Cardano led a crypto drop [[n1985]]. Coinbase's chief plans to hire 1,000 US workers [[n2030]], and Coinbase will offer 24/7 and perpetual-style futures in the US [[n6537]].
Playbook

Stay underweight spot crypto until the reserve bid shows up in price. The order is the bull case, but the price has moved through the level described as a November low [[n2023]]. Treat the equity proxies as one position: Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood trade as leveraged versions of the same risk appetite. The call changes if Bitcoin reclaims its 95,539.55 reference close from 2025-02-18 and IBIT holds its 54.47 USD reference from 2025-02-07 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).

flows.title: Capital Flows & Liquidity Framework: the curve says cuts, credit says wait
parts: Global Liquidity

Policy is pulling in two directions. Powell says the Fed is in no hurry to adjust rates [[n11257]], and Waller still sees two to three cuts this year [[n11158]]. The ECB has cut to 2.5% and says policy is becoming less restrictive [[n3463]][[n3468]]. Japan's 10-year yield is at its highest since 2008 on bets for BOJ hikes [[n5384]]. In China the liquidity drain is self-inflicted: a strategist says more bond issuance to keep yields up will drain liquidity from markets [[n4075]]. Trading plumbing is changing too. Nasdaq plans 24-hour trading five days a week [[n11249]], and the FT reports Nasdaq halted a high-speed trading service after regulatory pressure [[n11329]].
Rates & Dollar

The curve is the cleanest liquidity read. The 2Y closed at 3.89% and the 10Y at 4.22% at the prior close, with the 10Y-2Y spread at +33 bps, and over 20 observations the 2Y is down 40 bps and the 10Y down 27 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-10). The dollar index sits at 103.91 index points, down 3.82% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Duration is doing its job: TLT is up 1.99% over 20 sessions to 91.05 USD and IEF up 2.05% to 95.05 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).
Credit Check

Credit is the stress gauge that has not broken yet. HYG is 0.25% lower over 20 sessions at 79.15 USD, and LQD is up 1.08% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The pressure sits with the lenders. KRE is down 14.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), and fintech stocks fell as Wall Street worried about consumer spending and credit [[n6544]]. Bloomberg reports a private-credit pioneer dragged down by insults and indecision [[n9347]], even as Blackstone gains SEC approval for a new private-credit solution [[n6533]].
Equity & Fund Flows

Fund flows point to cash and to selective bets. Short-term bond ETFs are raking in billions amid recession alarm bells [[n4074]], and hedge funds have given up half of their 2025 gains in challenging markets, Goldman Sachs says [[n3958]]. Hedge funds cut China stocks for a fourth week [[n1564]], and Japanese investors sold foreign stocks in February [[n5390]]. In IPOs, Venture Global's flop wiped out $38 billion after listing [[n4085]], while JX Metals raised $3 billion in Japan's biggest IPO since SoftBank [[n4058]]. Dave Inc. announced a $50 million repurchase authorisation [[n4041]]. Retail traders are getting spooked, which is bad news for brokerage stocks [[n6573]]. For now the flow read is cautious: funds are de-risking, Venture Global's listing has flopped, and money is parking in short-term bonds. A reversal in that pattern would matter more than any single data print.
Portfolio Implication

Hold duration, keep equity exposure light into the shutdown and inflation tests, and favour defensives. XLP is up 4.20% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), and the curve's bull steepening (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-10) argues for owning IEF and TLT rather than holding cash alone. Treat the regional banks as the stress gauge: a KRE that stops falling would be the first sign that the flows have bottomed. Size the hedge rather than the thesis. The flow evidence says the dip is not yet over, so buy protection before the shutdown deadline rather than after it, and keep defensives as ballast while bond ETFs keep taking in money (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).

anticipatory.title: Shutdown weekend: the tail risk is being priced
parts: What Is Priced

Yahoo Finance put the odds of a shutdown this weekend at about 1 in 3 [[n11352]], Trump said it is possible but expected to be averted [[n11287]], and House Republicans aimed for a vote on Tuesday to avert it [[n11208]]. The dollar slipped back as markets mulled a shutdown [[n0509]].
Conditional Expression

A passed bill removes the weekend tail and favours the cyclicals that fell hardest, which is the bounce the bears would need to fade. A shutdown favours staples and Treasuries, where XLP is up 4.20% over 20 sessions and TLT is up 1.99% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).
Risk

Politics is the risk, not the arithmetic. Democrats are serious about a shutdown [[n10967]], and Hakeem Jeffries has rejected the shutdown plan from Mike Johnson [[n11238]]. The timing is the variable the market cannot model, since a vote on the day and a deal after the weekend are both live.

anticipatory.title: Inflation data: the Fed's next test
parts: What Is Priced

Reuters framed the week ahead as a test for the stock market on inflation data [[n0499]], and the curve already prices cuts: the 2Y is down 40 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-10). Waller sees two to three cuts this year [[n11158]], while Powell says the Fed is in no hurry [[n11257]].
Conditional Expression

A hot print pushes the 2Y back up and unwinds the bull steepening, which hurts long-duration growth. A soft print confirms the cut path and supports rate-sensitive names. Powell's openness to tweaking the dot plot [[n11235]] means the Fed may change its messaging before it changes rates.
Risk

The stagflation combination is the risk. Goldman's cut to US forecasts says tariff impacts are growing 'considerably more adverse' [[n10896]], so prices could firm while growth slows. The curve's move is the cleanest way to see the risk building (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-10).

anticipatory.title: US-China summit: the diplomacy option
parts: What Is Priced

Trump may meet Xi in China as soon as April, SCMP's insiders say [[n1556]], and Reuters reports the two sides discussing a Trump-Xi summit for June [[n1625]]. The Hang Seng is up 10.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), which suggests some of the diplomacy is already being bought.
Conditional Expression

A confirmed date favours China's internet and AI names, with KWEB up 9.29% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). A breakdown sends them back toward their early-February levels, and the port-fee retaliation [[n1623]] is the first thing to watch.
Risk

Summits slip, and the tariff tit-for-tat is already moving. China's fresh agriculture tariffs on Canada show how quickly retaliation spreads [[n1479]]. A summit that slips hands the trade back to the market's tariff worry, which is the reason to size it small.

anticipatory.title: BOJ in May: the hike the yen is already pricing
parts: What Is Priced

Sources say the BOJ could discuss a rate hike in May as inflation risks build [[n5310]], and Japan's 10-year yield is at its highest since 2008 on bets for hikes [[n5384]]. USD/JPY is down 2.79% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), so part of the hike is already in the currency.
Conditional Expression

A confirmed May hike pushes the yen higher and hits exporters, including Tokyo Electron, down 19.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). A delay gives the yen back its carry and supports the export names.
Risk

Growth is the constraint. Japan's fourth-quarter GDP was revised lower [[n3112]], so a hike into softness is the risk to watch. If the BOJ signal arrives while the Nikkei is still below its 39,066.53 reference close, the market will have priced the hike before the economy can carry it (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).

catalysts.title: $AVGO — AI guidance still has room
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Broadcom's AI revenue jumped 77% and the stock jumped with it [[n2988]], and CNBC reports strong guidance on AI growth powered the rise [[n2990]]. The thesis is that AI guidance is the most reliable forward number in semis right now, and the sector sell-off has pushed the price below what that guidance supports.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Broadcom closed at 184.45 USD, down 5.39% in the prior session and 17.97% over 20 sessions from 224.87 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The hurdle is the sector itself: SOXX is down 10.35% over 20 sessions, and Marvell's beat-and-tumble shows a beat is not enough [[n3008]].
Trade Expression

Buy the shares in tranches while the semis ETF stays below its 216.87 reference close from 2025-02-07 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The thesis is invalidated if Broadcom's next guidance cuts the AI number rather than raising it.

catalysts.title: $COST — the consumer is the risk
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

A quarter that missed on profit [[n2874]], and a stock that fell on cautious consumers and tariff threats [[n2996]], make the next guidance the catalyst and the consumer's response to tariffs. The thesis is that the miss is about margins, not a one-quarter blip.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Costco closed at 934.41 USD, down 3.10% in the prior session and 10.48% over 20 sessions from 1,043.81 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The hurdle is the stock's still-premium multiple, and the risk is that the miss proves to be a one-off in margin terms.
Trade Expression
Buy puts or a put spread into the next print. The view is invalidated if Costco reclaims its 1,043.81 reference and holds it through a full session cycle.

catalysts.title: $ORCL — the AI capex call is the bear case
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The sales miss [[n0504]] sits awkwardly with a chief executive who still expects AI-driven growth, and Niles's call that Oracle's AI capex will shrink [[n9179]] runs against that message. The catalyst is the next guidance. The thesis is that capex guidance will fall short of the growth the stock still assumes.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Oracle closed at 148.79 USD, down 4.11% in the prior session and 14.71% over 20 sessions from 174.46 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The risk is the data-center growth Oracle keeps touting [[n3126]], and a stock already down this far may not need much to rally.
Trade Expression
Bear put spread into the next print. The view is invalidated if Oracle reclaims its 174.46 reference close.

catalysts.title: $LLY — the emerging-market launch
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Eli Lilly plans to launch its weight-loss drug in emerging markets this year [[n4049]]. Roche is hiring a Novo executive to push into obesity drugs [[n9355]], and Novo's trial shares fell 6.3% [[n9327]], which leaves Lilly with the cleaner obesity story.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Eli Lilly closed at 829.76 USD, down 4.58% in the prior session and 5.53% over 20 sessions from 878.31 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The risk is that the stock trades on the next trial read rather than on launch timing.
Trade Expression
Accumulate in stages while the stock sits below its 878.31 reference close, and treat the thesis as broken if the emerging-market launch slips.

catalysts.title: $BABA — the Hong Kong AI rally
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Alibaba's new RISC-V chip is reported to hit the mark for China's tech ambitions [[n1568]], and mainland investors are buying Hong Kong stocks to play AI [[n1575]]. The catalyst is the AI competition and tariff commentary from Alibaba.com's president [[n1628]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Alibaba closed at 132.54 USD, down 5.75% in the prior session but up 28.05% over 20 sessions from 103.51 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The risk is the US-China channel, where a summit could slip [[n1556]] and retaliation is already moving [[n1623]].
Trade Expression
Own the ADR on pullbacks, with invalidation on a close back under its 103.51 reference from 2025-02-07 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).

catalysts.title: $RHM — the crowded defence rally
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Germany's refusal of joint defence Eurobonds [[n3609]] keeps the spending national, and hedge funds have made European defence stocks a home run [[n3613]]. The Economist reports armsmakers are tooling up as Germany's defence stocks go ballistic [[n3453]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Rheinmetall closed at 1,119.00 EUR, up 0.36% in the prior session and 53.08% over 20 sessions from 731.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The hurdle is crowding: a stock up that far in 20 sessions can fall as quickly.
Trade Expression
Hold rather than chase, and trim into strength. The view turns negative if the German spending plan is watered down, which would remove the fiscal leg of the trade.

retail_intro: Tesla is the dominant popular-narrative trade on March 10, a retail favourite whose drawdown the crowd blames on politics rather than cars, and it resembles the GameStop squeeze that Reuters still calls the 'GameStop effect' [[n6349]] as well as the Tesla and bitcoin manias of 2020 to 2021.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — bring back the CEO, buy the dip
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The crowd's story is simple and emotional. Tesla is a brand that was never supposed to fall this far, and what is breaking it is politics rather than the cars. Business Insider's line that the stock has been cut in half and investors want their CEO back [[n6604]] is the sentence retail repeats, because it puts the fix in one person. The anchor is the 361.62 close from early February, set against the 222.15 close of the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Against that reference the stock looks like a sale, which is what makes the dip feel obvious and unstoppable.
What Is Driving It

The hard evidence is the price. Tesla closed at 222.15 USD after a 15.43% fall in the prior session, the steepest drop in five years [[n9378]], and it is down 21.96% over five sessions and 38.57% over 20 sessions from 361.62 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Forbes calls it a pre-election low, with Musk's net worth down $144 billion [[n11348]]. Yahoo Finance reports the 45% fall from the record high as a 'gut check moment' [[n8793]]. Peers fell too, with less damage: Rivian closed at 10.96 USD, down 12.18% over 20 sessions, and Lucid at 2.08 USD, down 26.50% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The backdrop is a risk-off tape. The Nasdaq 100 fell 3.81% in the prior session and 9.59% over 20 sessions, the VIX closed at 27.86 and the 10-year yield is 4.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10; US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-10). The dollar index is down 3.82% over 20 sessions, which is the odd piece of the picture (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).
The Social Signal

Attention looks like protest and identity. Activists used 'Tesla Takedown' protests to fight job cuts by Musk and Trump [[n8083]], and by March 10 police were barricading Tesla cars and dealerships as anger rose [[n11338]]. CNN reports acts of vandalism against Tesla facilities as anger against Musk mounts [[n9343]]. Retail is splitting on the brand. Some are walking away, and Business Insider's piece is titled 'We're getting rid of our Tesla — and Elon Musk's politics have nothing to do with it' [[n9417]], while owners are rebranding their cars [[n8716]]. Others are buying the dip on the crowd's own line that investors want their CEO back [[n6604]]. Musk's counter-story is that the anti-Tesla protests are being astroturfed by Democratic megadonors George Soros and Reid Hoffman [[n6542]], and his supporters are likely to repeat it.
Historical Analog

The closest precedent is the GameStop squeeze. Reuters sees retail traders behind Eutelsat's 650% surge, which it calls the 'GameStop effect' [[n6349]], and Finance Magnates still dates the GameStop chaos five years back [[n6545]]. The mechanical similarity is the second wave, not the squeeze itself. In the first wave, institutions reprice a brand-name stock on a story. In the second, holders who refuse to sell turn their refusal into the trade. Tesla's first wave is the political repricing, and its second is the loyal owner who now sees a falling stock as a bargain. Trump Media is the nearer analogue on the politics: its stock has lost half its value since Inauguration Day [[n6593]], and its holders face the same question about whether to hold.
Smart Money View

Institutions split on direction, not pace. The bull case is that a stock down this far is a gut-check entry: Wall Street bulls are doubling down [[n8793]], and the New York Times argues tariffs could help Tesla by hurting its rivals more [[n1613]]. The bear case asks whether the core business still works. Reuters asks whether Musk's EV party is over [[n3143]], and Fortune says Tesla is flailing in China as BYD rises [[n9076]]. Hedge funds as a group are de-risking, having given up half of their 2025 gains in challenging markets, Goldman Sachs says [[n3958]]. The disagreement is whether the price is cheap or broken. Sales decide that, and Tesla sales plummeted 45% in Europe [[n3032]].
When the Narrative Breaks

The narrative breaks on observable levels and prints. The 20-session reference is 361.62, and the 222.15 close sits 38.57% under it (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Three triggers matter. First, another session like the 15.43% drop would turn buying into capitulation. Second, a continuing sales slump would make the brand argument hard to sell, and sales plummeted 45% in Europe [[n3032]]. Third, the broad tape. The Nasdaq 100 is down 9.59% over 20 sessions, and a VIX that keeps climbing past its 27.86 close would show that dip-buying is failing against a market-wide sell-off (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). Instrument risk is single-name concentration. Leveraged versions of the same risk show how far leverage has already been cut: TQQQ is down 27.70% over 20 sessions and SOXL 31.67% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10).

retail.title: Satellite stocks / ASTS — the Starlink rival bet
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The crowd's story is that Starlink proved the model and the next names are the rivals. CNBC reports a European Starlink rival's shares skyrocketed 390% in a week [[n3585]], and Reuters sees retail traders behind Eutelsat's 650% surge in the 'GameStop effect' [[n6349]]. In the US, Yahoo Finance asks whether AST SpaceMobile is the best emerging technology stock to buy now [[n6554]], and Motley Fool asks whether buying Rocket Lab today could set you up for life [[n6538]]. The hook is the next big thing everyone else missed.
Where It Breaks

The levels set the trigger. ASTS closed at 29.14 USD, down 12.75% in the prior session but up 9.92% over 20 sessions, and Rocket Lab closed at 17.12 USD, down 37.54% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). A close below ASTS's 26.51 reference from 2025-02-07 would take the stock back to its early-February level. Rocket Lab's Neutron news is a company-specific risk [[n6569]]. The instrument risk is size: these are small, high-beta names where one report can move the price more than the market does. Eutelsat's shares slipped as investors paused the rally on Ukraine prospects [[n6442]], which shows how fast the bid can stop.

retail.title: Dogecoin / DOGE — the meme coin that keeps coming back
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The meme-coin crowd still has a comeback story. A TradingView analysis asks whether Dogecoin's fate hinges on $0.16, breakout or breakdown [[n2034]], and another says it could shoot up to $2.74 [[n2005]]. A new meme coin, Cocoro, has launched from Dogecoin's IP rights holder [[n2041]], which is the new-ticket feeling the crowd is after. The category has been mocked and cratered. The memecoin market fell 56% from its December peak amid fading hype [[n6300]], and Trump's own meme coin is down 81% since launch [[n1928]]. Retail reads the lows as a second chance.
Where It Breaks

Price is the trigger. DOGE closed at 0.15 USD, down 8.19% in the prior session, 24.75% over five sessions and 38.60% over 20 sessions from 0.25 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-10). A close below the $0.16 level that the chart analysis discusses would confirm the breakdown case [[n2034]]. The instrument risk is that a meme coin has no earnings to anchor it, liquidity thins on the way down, and Bitcoin's 17.80% fall over 20 sessions removes the bid it needs (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-10).

retail.title: Oklo / OKLO — small reactors, big data-centre demand
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Nuclear is being sold as the new power story for AI, and the crowd is buying the small-reactor names. Alphabet's chief investment officer says the company aims to slash the cost of new nuclear through small reactor deployments [[n6525]], and the Trump administration aims to support small nuclear power [[n6594]]. The demand case is the data centre: PJM transmission growth has rebounded and data centres boost the outlook for future expansion [[n10921]]. Oklo, which closed its acquisition of the radioisotope producer Atomic Alchemy [[n6310]], is the name retail points to. The hook is simple: the grid needs power, and nuclear is power.
Where It Breaks

The levels are severe. OKLO closed at 23.69 USD, down 9.82% in the prior session, 19.37% over five sessions and 57.31% over 20 sessions from 55.49 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). NuScale is down 43.23% over 20 sessions and Nano Nuclear 28.50% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10), and uranium is weak too, with URA down 20.58% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-10). The break comes if the policy support the crowd is pricing [[n6594]] turns into a reversal, with the 55.49 close from early February as the bulls' reference. The instrument risk is a single-policy story, where a funding announcement can move the price more than the power demand does.
